biography.plain_text: Martin Harold Stott is a British businessman who founded Countrywide Grounds Maintenance. He and his family developed the Manchester business into a national network of more than fifty franchisees, providing commercial landscaping and winter services. The family sold the company to the Dwyer Group in 2017 after three decades of ownership.

long_biography.plain_text:
Martin Stott's grounds maintenance business combined local contractors with centrally negotiated national accounts. At Countrywide, head office handled invoicing for these contracts, while franchisees carried out the work. New operators trained at the company's Cheshire headquarters and alongside established franchisees, learning accounting, sales, employment requirements and practical maintenance.

That support extended to risk assessments, environmental policies and quality control. Two Midlands franchisees credited Countrywide's assistance when they joined forces to service Severn Trent Water, a contract neither could fulfil alone. The partners subsequently merged their franchises, bought four more territories and ran three operational depots.
